in_sanskrit.name: सत्यन
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Satya is a Sanskrit word meaning truth, reality, fact, and righteousness. It is a central concept in Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism, representing the moral order and the ultimate reality. Satyan is a compound of sat (truth) and yan (to exist, to be).

in_hindi.name: सत्यन
in_hindi.long_meaning: In Hindi, Satyan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Satya', which holds the same meaning as in Sanskrit. It is a common name in the Indian subcontinent.

in_tamil.name: சத்யன்
in_tamil.long_meaning: In Tamil, Satyan is translated as 'Kōzhi' (truth), 'Nipantanam' (truthfulness), and 'Sandōśam' (purity).

in_telugu.name: శత్యన్
in_telugu.long_meaning: In Telugu, Satyan is translated as 'Satya' (truth) and 'Hēmam' (gold). The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Satya', and the gold reference may symbolize the purity and value of truth.

in_marathi.name: Satyan
in_marathi.long_meaning: Satyan हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Satya’, meaning ‘Truth’ or ‘Reality’. In Hindu mythology, Satyan is associated with truthfulness, righteousness, and honesty. The name is considered auspicious and is given to boys to instill virtues of truth, honesty, and integrity.
